newsitem.title: UK: Futures rally, holiday stall physical coffee trade.
newsitem.headline: Futures rally, holiday stall physical coffee trade.

text.p: Physical coffee markets were virtually at a standstill on Thursday after another explosive rally in New York arabica futures sidelined many origin sellers, traders said.
Despite the May Day holiday across much of Europe, some traders were at their desk and roasters were also said to be keeping a close eye on New York.
Roasters might be forced to step up activity if they decided arabica futures would go much higher, traders added.
The industry still had substantial contracts to fix against New York's July while origins were said to be well fixed.
"There were little offers from the origins while roasters were waiting for the right moment to cover," one trader said.
Analysts said the lack of supply meant the current rally might continue until September -- even without a damaging frost in Brazil in June and July.
The next Central American and Colombian crop is not due until October at the earliest.
On Thursday July hit a new contract high of 218.25 cents a lb in early trade. By 1552 GMT, it was trading 7.60 up at 218 cents as bullish sentiment prevailed.
One London trader said the rally could have attracted some roaster and fund involvement but volume was rather light.
Traders said arabica offers were few and at steep levels with many origins well sold or holding back due to soaring New York values.
"Nobody is in a hurry to sell," said one Dutch trader.
There were some light forward sales of the next crop of washed arabicas for shipments early next year.

London's robusta futures still lagged behind New York, with the May/May arbitrage widening to a new record of $1.74 a lb. The robusta sector is well supplied and the market is bracing for large Indonesian arrivals.
A total of 791 five-tonne lots were tendered against LIFFE's May on Thursday at the start of the month-long notice period.
Traders said the level was surprisingly low given some 5,000 tonnes of coffee which were certified in April.
